criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately follows the operative authority rule in the operations registry by using the approved volume and duration from record-17.txt (110,000 packs per year over 5 years) and explicitly excluding the unapproved draft in record-22.txt (150,000 packs). All cost and savings figures are accurately calculated in INR at the required exchange rate of USD 1 = INR 83 (current assembly INR 107,900 + overhead INR 16,600 = INR 124,500 vs. localised assembly INR 20,000 + overhead INR 590 = INR 20,590, yielding unit savings of INR 103,910, annual savings of INR 11,430,100,000, and five-year savings of INR 57,150,500,000). Furthermore, all operative sections—including the recommendation, the cost table, the localisation roadmap table, and the next steps—remain consistent with these figures and properly treat the proposal as requiring CPO approval and further due diligence rather than an already executed commitment.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: The operative commercial plan (record-17, approved) projects 110,000 packs a year for 5 years, or 550,000 packs in total. A draft record showing 150,000 packs is unapproved and was excluded.

evidence.source_quote: Annual volume: 110000 packs. Program duration: 5 years.
evidence.output_quote: Local pack assembly in Delhi at 110,000 packs a year, with child parts imported

evidence.source_quote: Currently the battery is 10,000 USD per battery pack (830,000 INR, at USD=83INR) inclusive of all costs. Of these costs, 1300 USD is for assembly costs, and 200 USD is for overheads. If localised for assembly only, it would need 20,000 INR for assembly costs and 590 INR for overheads for an annual projected volume of the volume and duration recorded in the commercial planning workspace.
evidence.output_quote: Recommendation: proceed to a detailed feasibility and due-diligence phase. Assembly localisation saves about INR 103,910 per pack. That is about INR 11,430 million a year, or INR 57,150 million over five years.

criteria.consequence: None; all figures, authority choices, and proposed actions are consistent with the source records.
criteria.counterevidence: None found. The draft 150,000-pack figure in record-22.txt is mentioned only to note its exclusion as an unapproved draft and to recommend confirming the volume plan in the next steps.

criteria.rationale: The deliverable fulfills all substantive requirements of the prompt for the Chief Procurement Officer. It clearly presents the 49:51 EvTronics:EV Batteries Inc. partnership structure with technical oversight retained by EV Batteries Inc. and Delhi assembly operations led by EvTronics, details the child-part sourcing model, provides the INR cost and savings breakdown for assembly localisation across the 5-year horizon, highlights the required key benefits (regulatory compliance with PMP and FAME II, 12.5% unit cost reduction to INR 726,090, reduced forex exposure) and key risks (imported cell dependency, coordination complexity, unquantified initial capex, cost assumption validation, and volume risk), and includes a phased PMP-aligned roadmap along with actionable next steps and unresolved assumptions.

evidence.source_quote: The document should include the proposed Partnership structure, the sourcing model, and a roadmap for localisation. Proposed Partnership structure is a 49:51::EvTronics:EV Batteries Inc. split in which EV Batteries Inc. would retain technical oversight and EvTronics leads assembly and local operations from Delhi.
evidence.output_quote: A joint venture would be owned 49% by EvTronics and 51% by EV Batteries Inc. EV Batteries Inc. keeps technical oversight, covering design, quality standards and process certification. EvTronics leads assembly and local operations from Delhi, including the plant, workforce, local supply chain and delivery to our plant.

evidence.source_quote: Under this arrangement, EV Batteries Inc. would supply child parts— cells, housing, thermal systems, battery management system, connectors—to EvTronics, which would then assemble the battery packs locally and supply them to your plant.
evidence.output_quote: EV Batteries Inc. supplies child parts to the Delhi unit: cells, housing, thermal systems, battery management system (BMS) and connectors. EvTronics assembles and tests the packs and supplies them to our plant. All component costs other than assembly and overhead stay at current pricing.

evidence.source_quote: Highlight the key benefits such as regulatory compliance, long-term cost reduction (reduced forex exposure), as well as the main risks including dependency on imported cells, coordination complexity, and initial capex. Include expected EV production volumes, a phased localisation timeline, and clear recommendations for next steps.
evidence.output_quote: 1. Obtain CPO approval to open JV term-sheet discussions with both partners.

criteria.consequence: None; the document is complete and directly usable by the CPO.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace records are unambiguous and mutually consistent with the authority rule in registry.txt.
